summary:
What if anyone could explore the changing universe and learn to investigate it like an astronomer?

Project NADIR is an interactive astronomical observatory and educational planetarium powered by real NASA SPHEREx infrared observations.

Users can explore celestial objects, compare telescope images across time, investigate stellar motion, examine infrared spectra, and evaluate the scientific evidence behind possible discoveries.

NADIR combines a Time Machine for multi-epoch observations, scientific analysis with uncertainty estimates, and cinematic planetarium experiences called NADIR Journeys.

Our goal is to make astronomical research more accessible by transforming complex space telescope measurements into an intuitive, interactive experience without sacrificing scientific accuracy.
details:
Project NADIR — An Atlas of the Unseen

The Problem

NASA's SPHEREx mission is mapping the infrared sky, collecting observations that enable scientists to investigate celestial objects across wavelengths and time. However, exploring these observations often requires specialized astronomical software and familiarity with scientific data processing.

Project NADIR aims to make this information accessible while preserving the rigor of astronomical investigation.

Our Solution

NADIR is a browser-based astronomical observatory and educational planetarium that lets users explore the changing infrared universe.

Interactive Observatory: Users search astronomical objects or enter celestial coordinates, explore SPHEREx imagery, and examine sources using astronomical catalog overlays.

Time Machine: NADIR retrieves real observations across different dates and wavelengths. Users can blink between exposures, compare images, and investigate changes without fabricating intermediate observations.

Scientific Investigation: The application combines astrometric alignment, reference-star comparisons, source tracking, infrared spectroscopy, uncertainty estimates, and scientific quality flags.

For Barnard's Star, NADIR estimates apparent motion of approximately 10.1 ± 1.7 arcseconds per year. This result is classified as systematics-limited. Gaia information helped calibrate the systematic error allowance, so agreement with Gaia is a consistency check rather than independent validation.

The application also identifies candidate measurements that fail its scientific reliability checks, illustrating the importance of rejecting false positives.

NADIR Journeys: Users can experience a cinematic, data-driven planetarium show. Our first journey, "The Stars Are Not Still," explores Barnard's Star, proper motion, infrared observations, and the scientific process. Users can then investigate the underlying evidence themselves.

Experimental Research

We developed a prototype called Spectro-Temporal Inverse Reconstruction (STIR), exploring whether spatial, spectral, and temporal constraints can improve the reconstruction of astronomical sources.

STIR remains experimental. It has not demonstrated superiority over established reconstruction methods, and we do not claim new astronomical discoveries or proven super-resolution.

Technology

NADIR uses Python, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, Astropy, astronomical image-processing libraries, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.

The integrated application passed 109 Python tests and 15 JavaScript tests during development, with additional browser-level testing of its guided astronomy experience.

Impact and Creativity

NADIR combines scientific analysis with accessible storytelling. Instead of only displaying telescope images, it helps visitors understand how astronomers test hypotheses, evaluate uncertainty, and distinguish genuine evidence from instrumental artifacts.

Our goal is to support astronomy education, independent exploration, and reproducible scientific investigation.

Development Transparency

Challenge-specific application implementation began on November 13, 2026, before the official hackathon start. We contacted the organizers to clarify eligibility and preserved the original development history.

Large language model coding tools, including ChatGPT, OpenAI Codex, and Anthropic Claude Code, were extensively used to implement, test, and document the application. Their contributions are acknowledged separately in the repository and submission.
